questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Based on the above, if ‘J + K ÷ L − T × R’, then how is J related to L?
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’;
‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’;
‘A × B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’ and
‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’.
Based on the above, if ‘J + K ÷ L − T × R’, then how is J related to L?
questions.solution:
J is the mother of K, K is the daughter of L, L is the brother of T and T is the sister of R.

​

S, J is the Wife of L.

questions.question: What will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 6 ÷ 8 – 91 × 13 + 30 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
What will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?
6 ÷ 8 – 91 × 13 + 30 = ?
questions.solution:
Given equation: 6 ÷ 8 – 91 × 13 + 30 = ?

After interchanging the signs then:

⇒ 6 × 8 + 91 ÷ 13 - 30 = ? ⇒ ? = 6 × 8 + 7 - 30 ⇒ ? =  48 + 7 - 30 ⇒ ? = 55 - 30 = 25

questions.question: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some circles are rectangles. Some rectangles are squares. All squares are triangles. Conclusions: I. No circle is a triangle. II. Some rectangles are triangles. III. All rectangles are triangles.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some circles are rectangles.

Some rectangles are squares.

All squares are triangles.

Conclusions:

I. No circle is a triangle.

II. Some rectangles are triangles.

III. All rectangles are triangles.

options.text: Both conclusion I and II follow
options.html: Both conclusion I and II follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. No circle is a triangle. - False (because there is no direct relation given between circle and triangle, so it can be possible but not definite)

II. Some rectangles are triangles. - True (because Some rectangles are squares and All squares are triangles. So, Some rectangles are triangles it is definite)

III. All rectangles are triangles. - False (because Some rectangles are squares and All squares are triangles. So, All rectangles are triangles it is not definite)

options.html: Leg​

questions.solution:
From Dice 2 and Dice 3,

Opposite pairs: Nose → Eyes, Leg → Ear, Mouth →  Hand

So, 'Mouth' will be the opposite face of 'Hand'.
